deep.reconstruction:
The page is a narrow strip of very faint pencil notes, two lines of formulas with no words. The symbols are partly illegible, so any reading is tentative. The most plausible reading is a set of elementary trigonometric relations for a triangle, with letters a, b, c and α, β, γ.

Line 1, first group. Riemann writes (b/c)·cot(αβ) + (c/b)·cot(αγ) = 1/(bc) = sin(αα)/(sin(αβ)·sin(αγ)) = … . Here 'αβ' and 'αγ' most likely denote angles: either the angle between lines/sides labelled α and β, or simply the angles β and γ.

The structural core, which is certain as an identity and is my reading, is the triangle relation
  cot β + cot γ = sin(β+γ)/(sin β sin γ) = sin α/(sin β sin γ), with α+β+γ = π.
In a plane triangle with opposite sides a, b, c and area Δ, this equals a²/(2Δ) = 2R·a/(bc), where R is the circumradius. The weights b/c and c/b and the value 1/(bc) suggest the variables have been rescaled or normalized; the exact normalization cannot be recovered from the image. The trailing expression, transcribed as a·sin γ/(α·α·b·c), is consistent with rewriting sin α/(sin β sin γ) through the law of sines. This is my interpretation.

Line 1, second group. Riemann writes
  1 = sin b/(β sin a sin c) + sin a/(α sin b sin c) + sin c/(γ sin a sin b),
followed by '= a+b+c', a fragment read as '(2π−1)/(abc)' (more likely something like Σ/(abc)), and 'b'+c' = −1/(bc)'.

This is a weighted cyclic sum of the type Σ sin A/(sin B sin C). The unweighted sum equals 2(cot A + cot B + cot C) when A+B+C = π. If a, b, c are small spherical sides, then sin x ≈ x and the sum becomes (a²/α + b²/β + c²/γ)/(abc). That may be what the '…/(abc)' fragment records; this is my conjecture.

The relation b'+c' = −1/(bc) looks like a definition of auxiliary quantities b', c'. The primes could also be derivatives, but nothing on the page decides this.

Line 2. Riemann writes (b/c·cot(αβ) + b')² = a²/(b·sin²(αβ)) + p. This reads as completing a square: an expression containing the cotangent term plus the auxiliary b' is squared, and the result is a cosecant-squared term plus a remainder p. It parallels the elementary 1 + cot²x = 1/sin²x, i.e. (cot x)² + 1 = csc²x.

The purpose is unclear. It could be a computation with a quadratic form attached to a triangle (e.g. an ellipse or conic through the vertices, or a metric form), or a scratch computation in spherical/geodesic trigonometry. The previous page is part of a private German letter draft and gives no mathematical context. The next page is illegible.
errors: No step can be verified as erroneous, because the notation and normalization are not recoverable.
Taken literally with α, β, γ as angles of a triangle, (b/c)cot β + (c/b)cot γ = 1/(bc) is not an identity. It must rely on a normalization or definitions not visible on the strip.
Taken literally, '1 = Σ sin b/(β sin a sin c)' is not a general identity. It presupposes special meanings for α, β, γ (weights or coefficients), which are not stated.
The fragment '(2π−1)/(abc)' is almost certainly a misreading.
